messages:

Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecommerce.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmecommerce.com>

Subject: Re: Order form draft — indemnity section (redlines attached)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending the order form. Procurement has a handful of redlines in the indemnity and third-party claim sections; attached is our annotated PDF (acme_redlines_20270418.pdf). High level: Acme is pushing for a mutual indemnity for IP infringement claims, a shorter notice window (7 days), and a carve-in for open-source claims. They also want an explicit statement that Acme can take control of defense where they have primary liability.

We need confirmation on:
- Whether Redwood will accept a mutual defend-and-pay approach for 3rd-party IP claims.
- If Redwood can keep the notice window at 30 days (we normally require 30) and provide a limited exception for emergency claims.
- Our position on OSS-originated infringement (they want it excluded).

Can your legal team propose alternate language and indicate any deal-level exceptions we should escalate to commercial? Procurement is hoping to close the PO next week.

Attachment: acme_redlines_20270418.pdf (PDF)

Cheers,

Sasha Reed
Senior Sourcing Manager, AcmeCommerce

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order form draft — indemnity section (redlines attached)

Team — forwarding Acme's redlines. They want mutual defend-and-pay, a 7-day notice, and OSS carve-in. Procurement wants to close next week, so we need an operational stance + suggested redline options for commercial to present.

My suggested approach:
1) Prioritize: 
   - High risk: mutual defend-and-pay for third-party IP claims (major revenue/insurance exposure).
   - Medium: 7-day notice (operationally risky; we need evidence-handling time).
   - Low: OSS carve-in (we typically exclude claims arising solely from customer modifications or customer's data).
2) Propose three fallback options for commercial:
   - Option A (preferred): Right to defend with Greenwood insurance offset; 30-day notice; OSS carveout remains.
   - Option B (compromise): Mutual defend-and-pay but with obligation caps tied to order form value and insurance triggers.
   - Option C (concession): Permit Acme to assume defense if Redwood elects not to, with reimbursement and control-of-defence protections.

Karthik/Kim — can you draft sample language for Options A/B/C and a short risk memo (1-2 bullets each) we can share with procurement? Also flag any internal approvals needed for a deal-level cap.

Thanks — I can join the procurement call tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order form draft — indemnity section (redlines attached)

Marissa / Kim —

Draft language below for the three options. High-level notes follow.

Option A (Preferred — Redwood defends):
"Redwood Inference shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer against any third party claim alleging that Redwood's Services infringe any intellectual property rights of such third party, provided that Customer (i) promptly notifies Redwood in writing of any such claim, (ii) gives Redwood sole control of the defense and settlement of the claim, and (iii) cooperates with Redwood's reasonable requests in connection with the defense. Redwood's liability under this Section shall be limited to direct damages up to the total fees paid by Customer under the Order Form in the twelve months preceding the claim; this limit shall not apply to liabilities arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct."

Option B (Mutual / capped):
"Each party shall indemnify the other for third-party claims to the extent caused by its negligence or willful misconduct. For IP infringement claims, the parties agree to a mutual defend-and-pay framework subject to an aggregate cap equal to 12 months of fees paid under the Order Form and conditioned upon receipt of commercially reasonable evidence supporting the claim. Either party may elect to have primary control of the defense; if the indemnifying party assumes defense, it shall bear reasonable costs and the indemnified party shall cooperate."

Option C (Concession — customer defense control):
"Customer may assume control of the defense of any claim at its election, provided Customer (i) notifies Redwood promptly, (ii) conducts the defense at its own expense, and (iii) does not settle any claim that admits liability on behalf of Redwood without Redwood's prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld). Redwood shall reimburse Customer for reasonable expenses if indemnification obligations apply, subject to the cap described in Section X."

Risk bullets: 
- Mutual defend-and-pay increases near-term financial exposure; insurers may not cover third-party IP suits triggered by model outputs.
- 7-day notice is operationally infeasible for evidence collection; 30 days is industry standard for complex IP claims. Exception: allow shorter notice for claims involving data exfiltration or security incidents.
- OSS carve-in request is a conceptual red flag; recommend excluding OSS claims originating from customer-supplied code/data, but consider a narrow carve-in for pre-trained model components only if insurance coverage aligns.

Approvals: Any cap > 12 months of ARR or any carve-in for OSS will require Director-level legal + CRO signoff.

I'll prepare a tracked Word doc with these redlines and a one-paragraph memo for procurement. Back to you, Marissa, for commercial-facing language.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Inference Products
karthik@redwood.inference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sasha Reed <sasha.reed@acmecommerce.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecommerce.com>

Date: 2027-04-19T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form draft — indemnity section (redlines attached)

Sasha — thanks for the redlines and the quick turnaround. Attached is a proposed counter (rdw_counter_indemnity_20270419.docx) that presents three options for procurement: Redwood-preferred (Option A), a middle ground (Option B), and a concession pathway (Option C) with the approval gates called out.

TL;DR reply for procurement:
- We cannot accept a blanket 7-day notice. We can offer a 14-day expedited notice for incidents where Acme has operational evidence that immediate remediation is needed; otherwise 30 days.
- We will not broadly accept OSS carve-ins. We will accept a narrowly defined OSS-related claim only where the alleged infringement arises solely from model components provided by Redwood and where we have had prior notice of the specific OSS at onboarding.
- We prefer to retain primary defense for IP claims (Option A). If Acme insists on mutual defend-and-pay, we propose a cap tied to order form value and an insurance trigger (Option B).

Proposed next steps:
1) Procurement to pick Option A/B/C by EOD Tuesday 2027-04-20.
2) If Option B or C chosen, Procurement to confirm requested cap amount and any insurance/escrow proposals.
3) Redwood legal to prepare final tracked redlines and a 1-page memo describing approval path.

Sasha — I can join the procurement call tomorrow at 9am PT. If you accept Option A, we can finalize quickly. If you need the compromise, please advise the cap you want us to evaluate.

Attachment: rdw_counter_indemnity_20270419.docx (Word)

Best regards,

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
